newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Kennedy to propose raising cigarette tax.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Kennedy to propose raising cigarette tax.

text.p: Sen. Edward Kennedy, a Massachusetts Democrat, said Thursday he planned to offer an amendment to the Senate tax bill that would increase the cigarette tax by 23 cents per pack.

Kennedy released a letter from Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala that said the Clinton administration supported his proposal to use money raised from a tobacco tax increase for child health programs.
The tax would be in addition to the 20-cent cigarette tax increase already in the Senate tax bill. Kennedy acknowledged the proposal faced an "uphill battle" this week.
But Kennedy said with the administration's support, the tax increase had a better chance of being included in legislation later on.
"Because the President has long supported using tobacco revenue to fund important programs for children, I am writing to advise you that the Administration supports your amendment," Shalala wrote.
The Kennedy proposal would raise $15 billion, of which $12 billion would be used to fund children's health programs, and the other $3 billion would go toward deficit reduction.
